```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

The **NMSDE** package estimates the spectral density matrices of a collection
of $M$ stationary $P$-variate time series. It implements NMCSDE
(nonparametric multivariate collective spectral density estimation) and, as
a special case, the noncollective NMSDE estimator of Nezampour et al. (2024).

## The model in brief

For series $i$, the inverse spectral matrix is factored as
$f_i^{-1}(\omega) = G_i(\omega) G_i^*(\omega)$, where $G_i$ is a complex
lower-triangular Cholesky factor. Its $P^2$ real and imaginary components,
evaluated at the Fourier frequencies $\omega_k = k/T$, are collected in
$K \times M$ matrices $\Gamma_j$ and modelled as

$$\Gamma_j = B\,\Theta_j A_j^\top, \qquad j = 1, \dots, P^2,$$

where $B$ is a rich B-spline basis with $L$ functions, $\Theta_j$
($L \times R$) defines $R \ll L$ basis functions that are learned from the
data, and $A_j$ ($M \times R$) holds the scores of the $M$ series. The
*different bases* model has one $\Theta_j$ per component. The *common bases*
model uses a single $\Theta$ for all components.

The parameters minimize a penalized Whittle negative log-likelihood. The
minimization uses Newton-Raphson iterations with step halving, and the
smoothing parameter $\lambda$ can be updated within the iterations. Because
every estimate is rebuilt from a Cholesky factor, it is Hermitian and
positive definite.

## Data

`dat` contains collections of simulated bivariate series. Each series comes
from one of three VAR models, and the true models are in `datPar`. Each
collection is a list of $P \times T$ matrices, which is the input format of
`initial()`.

```{r}
library(NMSDE)
X <- dat$X2
length(X)        # M series
dim(X[[1]])      # P x T
table(datPar$modelPar2$rnd)   # generating model of each series
```

## Choosing the rank R

`initial()` computes the periodograms, the Nadaraya-Watson starting estimate
and the starting values of $(\Theta, A)$. Its `elbow` component helps to
choose $R$: it holds the within-cluster sum of squares of a hierarchical
clustering of the starting estimates.

```{r elbow, fig.height = 3.5}
init0 <- initial(X, nbasis = 10, R = 2)
plot(init0$elbow, type = "b", pch = 20, xlab = "Number of clusters",
     ylab = "Within-cluster sum of squares", main = "Elbow method")
```

The elbow at three clusters suggests $R = 3$.

## Fitting NMCSDE

We fit both variants. Supplying `tru` stores the true spectra so that we can
compare against them. With `update.lam = TRUE` (the default), $\lambda$ is
updated at every iteration and no grid search is needed.

```{r fit}
tru <- datPar$modelPar2
initD <- initial(X, nbasis = 10, R = 3, theta_P2 = TRUE,  tru = tru)  # different bases
initC <- initial(X, nbasis = 10, R = 3, theta_P2 = FALSE, tru = tru)  # common bases

fitD <- iterate(initD, lambda = 1, n.iter = 30, verbose = FALSE)
fitC <- iterate(initC, lambda = 1, n.iter = 30, verbose = FALSE)
c(different = fitD$r.iter, common = fitC$r.iter)   # parameter sets stored
```

`tA2G()` rebuilds the Cholesky components from the final parameters, and
`inChol2spec()` turns them into spectral matrices. Each spectral matrix is
stored as a vector of length $P^2$: the real parts of the lower triangle,
then the imaginary parts of the strictly lower triangle (see
`?Cholindexer`).

```{r spec}
spec_hat <- function(fit, init) {
  k <- fit$r.iter
  G <- tA2G(fit$thetas[[k]], fit$As[[k]], init)
  array(apply(G, 3, inChol2spec, init = init),
        dim = c(init$P^2, init$K, init$m))
}
specD <- spec_hat(fitD, initD)
specC <- spec_hat(fitC, initC)
specNW <- simplify2array(initD$NW)   # Nadaraya-Watson starting estimate

rel_err <- function(S, init) {
  mean(sapply(seq_len(init$m), function(i) {
    truth <- init$truspec[, , init$rnd[i]]
    sqrt(sum((S[, , i] - truth)^2) / sum(truth^2))
  }))
}
round(c(NW = rel_err(specNW, initD),
        NMCSDE.D = rel_err(specD, initD),
        NMCSDE.C = rel_err(specC, initC)), 3)
```

The next plot shows the estimated spectra of one series from each model,
with the true spectra as dashed lines. The four panels are the two auto
spectra, the real part of the cross-spectrum (co-spectrum) and its imaginary
part (quadrature spectrum).

```{r plot, fig.height = 6}
labs <- c("f11", "Re f21", "f22", "Im f21")
ser <- match(1:3, initD$rnd)     # first series generated by each model
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (j in 1:4) {
  rng <- range(specD[j, , ser], initD$truspec[j, , ])
  matplot(initD$omegas, specD[j, , ser], type = "l", lty = 1, col = 1:3,
          ylim = rng, xlab = "Frequency", ylab = "", main = labs[j])
  matlines(initD$omegas, initD$truspec[j, , 1:3], lty = 2, col = 1:3)
}
par(op)
```

`plot_sds(fitD, initD)` draws the same kind of plot for every series, one
page per series.

## Noncollective estimation

Setting `which.spec = i` in `iterate()` fits series $i$ on its own. This
gives the noncollective NMSDE estimate, which can be compared with the
collective one.

```{r separate}
fit1 <- iterate(initD, lambda = 1, n.iter = 30, which.spec = 1, verbose = FALSE)
G1 <- tA2G(fit1$thetas[[fit1$r.iter]], fit1$As[[fit1$r.iter]], initD)
spec1 <- inChol2spec(G1[, , 1], initD)
truth1 <- initD$truspec[, , initD$rnd[1]]
round(c(separate = sqrt(sum((spec1 - truth1)^2) / sum(truth1^2)),
        collective = sqrt(sum((specD[, , 1] - truth1)^2) / sum(truth1^2))), 3)
```

## Clustering the series

The fitted scores $A_j$ give a low-dimensional summary of each series in
the common subspace, so they are a natural input for clustering. Here we
apply hierarchical clustering with Ward's method to the standardized scores,
which is also the default in `launch_app()`. Log spectra work as well.
Distances between raw spectra are dominated by a few large peaks, so they
separate the groups less well.

```{r cluster, fig.height = 3.5}
scores <- fitD$As[[fitD$r.iter]]                   # M x R x P^2
feat <- scale(matrix(scores, nrow = initD$m))       # M x (R P^2)
hc <- hclust(dist(feat), method = "ward.D2")
cl <- cutree(hc, k = 3)
table(cluster = cl, model = initD$rnd)
plot(hc, labels = initD$rnd, main = "Series labelled by generating model",
     xlab = "", sub = "")
```

## Bootstrap confidence intervals

`NMSDEBoot()` implements a multivariate spectral bootstrap. It simulates new
discrete Fourier transforms from a fitted spectrum, refits the model and
returns the bootstrap spectra. Pointwise percentile intervals follow from
`quantile()`. The code below is not run here because it refits the model
`nBoot` times.

```{r boot, eval = FALSE}
boot <- NMSDEBoot(specD, nBoot = 200, init = initD, lambda = 1,
                  update_lam = TRUE, method = "collective")
# 95% pointwise interval of f11 for series 1
ci <- apply(boot[[1]][, , 1], 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
```

## Interactive application

`launch_app()` opens a 'shiny' application with the same steps (data
description, elbow plot, basis functions, fitting and clustering) for the
bundled, simulated or uploaded data.

## References

Nezampour, S., Nematollahi, A., Krafty, R. T. and Maadooliat, M. (2024). A
new approach to nonparametric estimation of multivariate spectral density
function using basis expansion. *Computational Statistics*, 39, 3625–3641.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/s00180-023-01451-4>

Maadooliat, M., Sun, Y. and Chen, T. (2018). Nonparametric collective
spectral density estimation with an application to clustering the brain
signals. *Statistics in Medicine*, 37(30), 4789–4806.
<https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.7972>

Berkowitz, J. and Diebold, F. X. (1998). Bootstrapping multivariate spectra.
*Review of Economics and Statistics*, 80(4), 664–666.
